brief: 6 quiet decisions that kill startups — and the founders that survived each one.

slots.body: Most failures don't come from bold bets. They come from silent choices made when no one was watching.

slots.title: Hiring Fast to Fill Seats
slots.body: A YC founder scaled to fifty people in weeks. The wrong hires burned cash and morale.
slots.calloutBody: Interview for values alignment first. Skills can be taught; culture cannot.

slots.title: Chasing Growth Ignoring Economics
slots.body: A SaaS founder spent heavily on ads. Revenue soared, but margins stayed dangerously negative.
slots.calloutBody: Model unit economics before scaling. Profitability is a feature, not a bug.

slots.title: Delaying Hard Founder Talks
slots.body: Two founders avoided equity discussions for years. Resentment quietly killed their partnership and product.
slots.calloutBody: Address equity and roles in month one. Silence compounds into divorce.

slots.title: Building in Stealth Too Long
slots.body: A fintech founder built for eighteen months. Launch day revealed nobody wanted the product.
slots.calloutBody: Sell before you build. Customer conversations de-risk your roadmap faster than code.

slots.title: Copying Competitors Feature by Feature
slots.body: One founder chased every rival update. Users forgot why the product existed at all.
slots.calloutBody: Build for your ideal customer, not your competitor's changelog. Differentiation wins.

slots.title: Overcapitalizing Before Product Fit
slots.body: A well-funded founder hired a massive team. Dilution and burn killed optionality within months.
slots.calloutBody: Raise what you need for eighteen months. Capital is a tool, not a trophy.

slots.body: The best founders don't avoid hard decisions. They make them loud, early, and with data.
